jobs.title: Senior Director, GTM Strategy and Operations
jobs.excerpt: About Hello Heart:Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.
jobs.description:
About Hello Heart:

Hello Heart is on a mission to make heart attacks a thing of the past.

We’re an AI company focused exclusively on heart health, building a platform that predicts and prevents cardiac events before they happen—identifying risk up to 10 days in advance versus 10 years in traditional clinical models.

This is already working at scale. Hello Heart has been shown to reduce inpatient hospital days by 47% and deliver ~$1,800 in annual savings per member. Hello Heart is the cardiac prevention partner to over 80% of large U.S. health plans and serves hundreds of public and private employers.

We’re defining how the #1 cause of death—heart disease—is managed in the AI era. Join us.

About the Role

Hello Heart is seeking a Senior Director, GTM Strategy & Operations to help scale how we bring major roadmap investments, new products, new market opportunities, and strategic growth initiatives to life. This role sits at the center of Client Strategy & Growth, Client Experience, Product, Marketing, Operations, Finance, Legal, Enablement, and our Product & Engineering teams in Tel Aviv. The ideal candidate is a highly strategic yet hands-on operator who can translate ambitious ideas into executable plans, drive alignment across executive stakeholders, and ensure Hello Heart's most important initiatives successfully move from concept to commercialization.

This is not a traditional project management role. We are looking for an enterprise problem solver and business athlete who thrives in ambiguity, influences without authority, and can partner effectively with senior leaders to turn strategy into measurable business outcomes. Success in this role requires equal parts strategic thinking, commercial judgment, operational excellence, cross-functional leadership, and the ability to leverage AI to improve execution, accelerate decision-making, and increase organizational efficiency. This individual will help shape how Hello Heart launches new capabilities, evolves go-to-market motions, scales commercialization practices, and executes high-impact strategic initiatives across the company.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the company's biggest new product launches and growth projects.
  • Turn big ideas and leadership goals into clear, step-by-step plans.
  • Work closely with teams across the company, including teams in Tel Aviv, to make sure everyone is ready for new launches.
  • Help leaders make smart decisions by pointing out risks and choices.
  • Fix problems and remove roadblocks to keep projects moving forward.
  • Create simple guides and rules so the company can launch new products smoothly every time.
  • Use AI tools to work faster, save time, and help the team make better decisions.
  • Provide executive leadership with clear, actionable reports to facilitate precise decision-making.

Qualifications

  • 10+ years of experience in business, consulting, or healthcare technology.
  • Proven success leading projects at scale with many different teams and leaders.
  • Experience bringing new products or services to market.
  • Great problem-solving skills and the ability to find smart solutions to tough business issues.
  • Ability to build trust with leadership and help drive consensus on major decisions.
  • Strong understanding of how business choices affect customers and company success.
  • Master at staying organized and keeping projects moving even when things are ambiguous and changing fast.
  • Excellent communication skills to explain complicated ideas simply.
  • Experience working with startup companies and international teams, like developers in Tel Aviv.
  • Skilled at using AI tools to get work done faster and smarter.
  • Experience in digital healthcare, health insurance, or consulting is highly desired.
  • Having an MBA or a similar advanced business degree is advantageous but not required.
  • Ability to travel 30-35% of the time

The US base salary range for this full-time position is $217,000.00 to $235,000.00. Salary ranges are determined by role and level. Compensation is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Please note that the compensation details listed in US role postings reflect the annual salary only and do not include equity or benefits.

Hello Heart has a positive, diverse, and supportive culture - we look for people who are collaborative, creative, and courageous. Oh, and if you want to see some recent evidence of the fun things we do at Hello Heart, check out our Instagram page.

jobs.description:
About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups representing 1.8M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, one of the fastest-growing companies in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

Role Overview

We're looking for a Manager, Collections to lead the day-to-day operations of our supplier commission revenue and collections function for hotels and rental cars. In this role, you'll own the execution of invoicing, collections, and reconciliation processes, manage a team of specialists, and drive continuous improvement to protect and grow Engine's commission revenue.

This is a hands-on management role focused on operational excellence, accuracy, and cash flow optimization. You'll work closely with Accounting, Finance, Supply, and external hotel and supplier partners to ensure Engine captures every dollar earned as we scale.

Key Responsibilities

  • Team Leadership: Manage, coach, and develop a team of commission collections specialists. Set clear goals, hold the team accountable to KPIs, and support day-to-day performance and career growth.
  • Operational Ownership: Oversee end-to-end invoicing, collections, and reconciliation of hotel and supplier commission activity, ensuring accuracy and timely processing each month.
  • Cash Application & GL Accuracy: Coordinate with Accounts Receivable Manager to ensure commission cash receipts are posted timely and accurately to the General Ledger, and that AR Aging reports are maintained and reviewed regularly.
  • Reconciliation: Perform and coordinate reconciliations post invoice together with Reconciliation Manager across high-volume commission and incentive payment datasets to validate completeness and identify variances, including invoice adjustments and credits.
  • Process Improvement: Identify and implement improvements to invoicing, cash application, and reporting workflows - including automation opportunities - to reduce manual effort and improve recovery rates.
  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate with Accounting, Finance, Sales, Accounts Receivable, Reconciliation, Groups Contracting, Data Analysts, Member Support and Supply to ensure monthly commission and incentive revenue is accurate, and to investigate month-over-month fluctuations.
  • External Communication: Communicate directly with hotel and supplier representatives to resolve discrepancies, follow up on outstanding payments, and maintain strong working relationships.
  • Tools & Systems: Manage third-party tools and processes that support hotel invoicing and payment activities.
  • Reporting: Track and report on key metrics (collection %, dispute rates, DSO, aging) to senior leadership, and flag risks that could lead to revenue leakage.
  • Special Projects: Contribute to ad-hoc projects and cross-functional initiatives as business needs evolve.

Qualifications

  • 8+ years of experience in commission collections, accounts receivable, or operations, with at least 5+ years of direct people management experience.
  • Hotel, travel supplier, or related industry experience is a plus.
  • Solid financial acumen and understanding of AR, cash application, and GL processes. Accounting or Finance degree preferred.
  • Strong communicator, comfortable working with both internal cross-functional partners and external hotel/supplier contacts.
  • Experience with ERP systems (NetSuite preferred; Salesforce a plus).
  • Advanced Excel and Google Sheets skills; proficient across Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.
  • Detail-oriented, organized, and able to manage competing priorities across a monthly close cycle.

Applications for this role will be accepted through 12/11/2026 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, all roles receive equity. Depending on the role, total compensation may also include an annual bonus. Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range
$83,000—$115,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation
We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

  • Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with equity for all employees. Some roles are also eligible for bonuses or commissions.
  • Benefits: Check out our full list at
  • Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more

Unit 42 - Unit 42 Consulting is Palo Alto Network's security advisory team. Our team is composed of recognized experts and incident responders with deep technical expertise and experience in investigations, data breach response, digital forensics, and information security.   • Demonstrated experience leading complex technical engagements and interfacing directly with clients and stakeholders.

  • Proficiency in host-based forensics, data breach response, and network traffic analysis.

  • Hands-on experience with forensic tools such as EnCase, FTK, X-Ways, SIFT, Splunk, Volatility, or similar technologies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in a relevant technical field.

  • Strong executive presence with experience presenting complex technical concepts to C-suite stakeholders.

  • Established external presence through public speaking, conference presentations, or industry publications.

  • Relevant industry certifications such as GIAC (GCFA, GCFE, GNFA), CISSP, or similar.

Our Commitment

We’re trailblazers that dream big, take risks, and challenge cybersecurity’s status quo. It’s simple: we can’t accomplish our mission without diverse teams innovating, together.

jobs.description:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart. 

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Network Architect is responsible for the discovery, architecture, design, engineering, and implementation of Voyager's enterprise network infrastructure across corporate offices, engineering environments, manufacturing facilities, secure environments, newly acquired companies, and mission-support locations.

Reporting to the Director of Networking, this role serves as a senior technical authority responsible for translating business, cybersecurity, compliance, and operational requirements into secure, scalable, resilient, and supportable network solutions.

The Network Architect will work across the complete network lifecycle - from current-state discovery and assessment through target-state architecture, detailed engineering, implementation, migration, testing, documentation, and operational transition. The successful candidate will help establish repeatable enterprise standards while supporting the unique mission and technical requirements of Voyager's classified and non-classified distributed aerospace, defense, and space technology environments. This role will require a minimum of an active TS / Top Secret Clearance with SCI Eligibility or TS/SCI upon hire

Responsibilities

Network Discovery & Assessment

  • Lead technical discovery and current-state assessments across Voyager facilities, newly acquired companies, and other environments being integrated into the enterprise.
  • Discover and document existing network topology, circuits, routing, switching, wireless, firewall boundaries, VPN connectivity, VLANs, IP addressing, segmentation, DNS/DHCP, network services, monitoring, and dependencies.
  • Identify undocumented infrastructure, architectural inconsistencies, single points of failure, capacity constraints, security concerns, technical debt, and lifecycle risks.
  • Develop current-state and target-state network diagrams, gap assessments, remediation plans, and migration recommendations.
  • Work with site personnel, engineering teams, cybersecurity, IT operations, vendors, carriers, and other stakeholders to establish an authoritative understanding of each environment.

Enterprise Network Architecture & Engineering

  • Design secure, scalable, highly available enterprise architectures for LAN, WAN, wireless, SD-WAN, internet edge, VPN, remote access, routing, switching, network segmentation, and related network services.
  • Develop and maintain enterprise network standards, reference architectures, engineering patterns, configuration standards, and technology roadmaps.
  • Produce high-level and low-level designs, logical and physical diagrams, implementation plans, bills of material, addressing strategies, VLAN/VRF designs, routing designs, and resiliency models.
  • Establish standardized architectural patterns that can be reused across Voyager while accommodating mission-specific and regulated-environment requirements.
  • Evaluate existing and emerging networking technologies and make technical recommendations based on capability, security, scalability, interoperability, lifecycle, and cost.

Network Build, Integration & Modernization

  • Provide hands-on engineering leadership during network builds, site activations, office expansions, technology refreshes, migrations, and acquisition integrations.
  • Design and support the transition of legacy or independently operated networks into Voyager enterprise architecture.
  • Develop migration strategies that minimize operational impact and provide clear rollback, validation, and acceptance criteria.
  • Coordinate circuit provisioning, carrier connectivity, network hardware deployment, configuration, cutover, and testing.
  • Validate routing, redundancy, failover, segmentation, security policy enforcement, application connectivity, and overall network performance following implementation.
  • Help develop templates, automation, and repeatable deployment methods to improve the speed and consistency of network delivery.

Security, Compliance & Resilience

  • Partner closely with Cybersecurity to incorporate Zero Trust, network segmentation, access control, logging, secure remote access, and least-privilege principles into network architecture.
  • Design network solutions that support Voyager's CMMC, CUI, ITAR/EAR, government, and other applicable regulatory and contractual requirements.
  • Support implementation of firewalls, VPN, network access control, security zones, enclave boundaries, segmentation, and network security monitoring.
  • Maintain architecture diagrams, design records, configuration standards, change documentation, and other technical evidence required to support audit and compliance activities.
  • Incorporate high availability, disaster recovery, business continuity, and operational resilience into network designs.

Technical Leadership & Operations

  • Serve as a senior escalation point for complex network engineering and architecture issues.
  • Lead or support root-cause analysis for significant network incidents and translate lessons learned into architectural or engineering improvements.
  • Provide technical direction and mentorship to Network Engineers and other infrastructure personnel without requiring direct personnel management.
  • Partner with Network Engineering, Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Cloud, IT Operations, application teams, and business stakeholders to deliver end-to-end solutions.
  • Work with vendors, managed service providers, telecommunications carriers, and technology partners on architecture, design, implementation, troubleshooting, and lifecycle planning.
  • Maintain accurate as-built documentation and diagrams and ensure completed projects transition cleanly into operational support.

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

Required Qualifications

  • Approximately 8+ years of progressive enterprise networking experience, with substantial experience performing senior network engineering and/or architecture responsibilities.
  • Expert-level knowledge of enterprise routing and switching, LAN/WAN, wireless, firewalls, VPN, internet connectivity, DNS/DHCP, IP addressing, network segmentation, and network monitoring.
  • Strong understanding of routing protocols and enterprise network design principles, including technologies such as BGP and OSPF, redundancy, high availability, QoS, and resilient network design.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing networks across multiple geographically distributed sites.
  • Experience performing network discovery, current-state assessments, architecture development, modernization, migration, and implementation.
  • Ability to take a project from business or technical requirement through architecture, detailed engineering, implementation, testing, and operational handoff.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills with the ability to diagnose complex problems spanning multiple network and infrastructure domains.
  • Ability to develop professional network diagrams, design documentation, implementation plans, standards, and technical recommendations.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, leadership, vendors, and business stakeholders.
  • U.S. Person status as required for applicable ITAR/export-controlled work.
  • Requires a minimum of a TS / Top Secret Clearance with SCI Eligibility or TS/SCI upon hire

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting aerospace, defense, government, advanced manufacturing, or other highly regulated environments.
  • Experience integrating networks associated with acquisitions, mergers, new facilities, or previously independent business units.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise technologies from vendors such as Cisco, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Aruba, Juniper, Meraki, Zscaler, or comparable platforms.
  • Experience with SD-WAN, network access control, enterprise IPAM/DNS/DHCP, cloud networking, and hybrid connectivity.
  • Experience with Microsoft Azure/Azure Government, GCC High, or other secure cloud and collaboration environments.
  • Experience with network automation, configuration templates, APIs, scripting, infrastructure-as-code, or automated documentation.
  • Relevant industry certifications such as CCNP, CCIE, JNCIP, PCNSE, Security+, CISSP, or comparable certifications.
  • Active U.S. Government security clearance required based on final position scope.

The good faith base salary rangefor this role is$170,000 - $190,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Understand each brand's identity, engagement goals, and constraints. Build the agentic workflows, prompts, reference libraries, and guardrails that produce work the brand is proud to send.
  • Set the creative bar. When a customer asks "can your platform make an email that looks like this," you're the person who makes it look like that. You'll produce the creative work that turns curiosity into conviction and proves what's possible.
  • Drive performance, not just aesthetics. Partner with customers on A/B tests, iterate on creative based on results, and build the playbook for what drives opens, clicks, and conversions, and reliably lands in the inbox, when AI is in the loop.
  • Shape the product. As the creative voice closest to product and engineering, you'll spot friction, refine workflows, and help shape model behavior to directly influence what we build next!
  • Define the playbook. Document patterns that work, share them with the team, and build the body of knowledge that lets us scale taste across every customer we onboard.

What You Bring

  • A portfolio that does the talking. Real lifecycle programs, real email campaigns, real product launches. Ideally with AI integrated into the workflow, but the bar is craft. If your work is exceptional, we want to see it. (Applications without a portfolio link will not be reviewed.)
  • Deep email design experience. You've designed hundreds of emails across lifecycle programs (onboarding, nurture, retention, win-back) and you have sharp opinions about layout, hierarchy, and what renders well across clients and devices. Comfortable getting into the code and build of an email is a plus.
  • Deep AI fluency. You don't need us to teach you what's new. You're already testing the latest image and generative models the week they drop, you're stringing them together in node based UIs, you have strong opinions about which ones get which jobs, and you know how to push them past their defaults to hit a specific look.
  • Enterprise client instincts. You've worked directly with sophisticated marketing teams, in-house, agency, or consultancy, and you know how to navigate brand reviews, legal, and the politics of getting work approved.
  • Lifecycle marketing literacy. You understand the difference between an email that wins a design award and one that hits an engagement or revenue target, and you can hold both standards at once.
  • Taste. This is the hardest one to write a bullet for, so we'll just say it: you have it, your portfolio shows it, and you can articulate why something works.

Why Hightouch?

You'll be the creative center of gravity for a product that's actively defining a category. The brands you'll work with are the ones you already follow. The team you'll join, Product, Engineering, Solutions, Design, ships fast and treats craft as a non-negotiable. And the work you do will compound: every workflow you build, every customer you ship for, makes the next one easier.

If you've been waiting for the moment to bet on AI in lifecycle marketing before it's obvious, this is it.

Compensation

$140,000-$180,000 USD per year, location-independent. Top of band is reserved for candidates with proven enterprise creative leadership and a portfolio that sets the bar. We also offer meaningful equity in the form of ISO options, with early exercise and a 10-year post-termination exercise window.

E-Verify Statement

Hightouch participates in E-Verify. After you join the team, we'll verify your eligibility to work in the U.S. by submitting information from your Form I-9 to the Social Security Administration and, if needed, the Department of Homeland Security. This process happens post-hire only — we never use E-Verify to pre-screen applicants.

jobs.excerpt: Thematic is a customer intelligence platform that helps enterprise CX, Voice of Customer and Customer Insights teams turn fragmented customer feedback into reliable, actionable insights.
jobs.description:
Thematic is a customer intelligence platform that helps enterprise CX, Voice of Customer and Customer Insights teams turn fragmented customer feedback into reliable, actionable insights.

By unifying surveys, tickets, calls, reviews and social data into a single, traceable source of customer truth, we enable organizations to confidently understand and act on customer signals. This grounded layer powers dashboards, teams and AI agents, delivering measurable outcomes such as faster time to insight, significant NPS improvements, reduced call volumes and strong ROI.

We integrate with existing CX stacks like Medallia and Qualtrics, data warehouses like Snowflake and BigQuery, and AI assistants like Copilot, Gemini and Claude.

Thematic powers CX programs at companies such as DoorDash, Woolworths and Mitsubishi. We are a team of around 20 people, profitable, and selling to enterprises across the US, Australia, New Zealand and Asia.

The role

We are growing our presence in Southeast Asia and adding dedicated coverage for the region. You will own it, reporting directly to our CEO.

It is not a cold start. We already have active enterprise opportunities in Singapore and the region in progress. What we do not yet have is someone here full time to convert them.

Here is how we see the role, although it is just a start. Depending on your success, it can evolve quickly.

  • Territory spans the SEA region, with Singapore as your base
  • Own a revenue number and build the pipeline to hit it
  • Own the full sales cycle, at least initially: prospecting, qualifying, closing
  • Create proposals and negotiate pricing
  • Some inbound leads and customer referrals exist, but expect to generate most of your own pipeline
  • Run local personalized outbound campaigns
  • Attend events and work warm intros, qualifying consultatively and building the business case with your buyer
  • Build relationships with existing customers and help renew and expand usage
  • Bring in our product specialists and data scientists as you need them
  • Customers are supported by our customer success team

Requirements

  • Based in Singapore with existing right to work here. We cannot sponsor a pass.
  • Five or more years closing full cycle B2B SaaS deals as an account executive
  • Sold into enterprise accounts through Singapore procurement and security review, and can walk us through one
  • Sold a considered, multi-stakeholder product where you built a business case rather than pitched features
  • Closed business in at least two SEA markets
  • Generated at least half your own pipeline in a recent role
  • Comfortable being the first and only person in market, working with a team mostly in New Zealand time, a few hours ahead of Singapore
  • Good CRM hygiene. We run on Pipedrive and expect it kept current.
  • Able to travel up to 20% within the region
  • You use AI in your daily sales work and can show us how

Nice to have: experience in CX, Voice of Customer, insights or market research, and experience at a company under 50 people.


How we work

Our values are Transparency, Ambition, Collaboration and Ownership. We are remote, we are direct with each other, and we expect people to run their own patch.

Benefits

Let's be direct about this. Our base is modest compared to a Salesforce or a Qualtrics. We are a 20-person profitable company, not a funded one burning through a round, and we pay from revenue. What we can offer instead is real equity, an uncapped commission scheme with no ceiling, and a territory that is entirely yours.

  • Base salary SGD 85K to 95K depending on experience
  • Uncapped commission under Thematic's sales commission scheme: 10% of recognized revenue, rising to 12.5% above target and 15% above 125% of target
  • Annual target of SGD 500K, prorated in your first year to reflect ramp. On-target earnings of approximately SGD 135K to 145K.
  • Multi-year contracts are recognized at full value at signature, so strong deals compound quickly
  • Stock options. This is a real allocation, not a token one.
  • 20 days paid time off per year
  • Work from home allowance of SGD 250 per month
  • Employee development programs
  • Remote with flexible hours. Work late, work early, it is up to you how you plan your week.
  • Annual team retreat in New Zealand.

Why take this over a bigger name

  • You own Southeast Asia. Not a slice of it, not a named account list handed down to you.
  • You report to the CEO. Pricing decisions, deal structure and territory strategy get answered the same day, by the person who can actually decide.
  • There is pipeline waiting, including active enterprise opportunities in Singapore and referrals from existing customers.
  • We are profitable and have been for years.
  • Our customers include DoorDash, Woolworths and Mitsubishi, so you are not selling an unproven product.

How to apply

Applicants must have valid work authorization in Singapore.

Apply through Workable and include the following two answers.

  1. In a few sentences: how would you approach opening a market where we have early enterprise pipeline but no local presence yet?
  2. In up to five sentences: describe one thing you have automated or built with AI in your own sales work. Name the tool, what it does, roughly how often you use it, and what it replaced. Generic answers will not progress.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager
jobs.excerpt: Who we are At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes.
jobs.description:
Who we are

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.

.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions!

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings.

.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Senior Engineering Manager.

About the job

As a Senior Engineering Manager in Communication Identity Domain, you will lead the engineering teams behind Porting, Hosting, and A2P Messaging. Your teams own the products that let customers bring their own numbers onto Twilio (Porting), enable existing numbers for messaging without a full port (Hosting), and register and operate compliant Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging campaigns at scale — the gateway that determines whether a customer's messages actually reach their end users' handsets. Porting and Hosting are high-value, white-glove transactions: each one touches an existing customer's live production number, or a prospective customer's number that already works elsewhere and needs to keep working seamlessly through the transition. That makes operational maturity a core part of the value we deliver — precise execution, clear communication, and dependable outcomes are what earn a customer's trust in the Communication Identity Domain. Delivering on that requires deep, reliable integration with a broad ecosystem of carriers, aggregators, industry registries and the expertise to orchestrate that complexity into a smooth, trustworthy experience for the customer. It also means investing in efficient, well-instrumented Ops Tooling that gives your team and our internal support organizations clear visibility into every port, hosting activation, and campaign — so issues are caught and resolved quickly, and operational excellence scales with the business. You will own the people strategy, delivery execution, and stakeholder relationships for a team responsible for the trust-building work of moving and activating phone numbers for existing and prospective customers.

You will be expected to champion AI-driven development practices, ensuring your engineers adopt LLMs and agentic tools to accelerate delivery, improve quality, and stay at the forefront of modern software engineering. Your mission is to build a high-performing team that consistently ships reliable, customer-obsessed products - while balancing the competing demands of external product commitments, internal platform obligations, and operational tooling investments.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • DRAW THE OWL: Own the delivery roadmap for the Communication Identity Domain, including customer-facing services, internal platform APIs, and Ops Tooling. Partner with Principal and Staff Engineers to translate long-term technical strategy into executable quarterly plans and measurable outcomes.
  • ACCELERATE WITH AI: Drive the adoption of AI coding assistants (GitHub Copilot, Anthropic Claude, or internal LLMs) within your team. Set expectations for AI-augmented workflows, measure the impact on team velocity, and create the psychological safety for engineers to experiment with new tools.
  • BE AN OWNER: Take full accountability for your team’s operational excellence, including system reliability, incident response, on-call health, and security posture. Make high-judgment calls that balance speed, quality, and risk.
  • WEAR THE CUSTOMER’S SHOES: Serve two customer bases with equal rigor. For external customers, partner with Product Management to ensure communication identity workflows are seamless and developer-friendly. For internal customers, proactively engage with dependent engineering teams to understand their needs, gather feedback on your team’s APIs and Ops Tooling, and ensure your platform enables them to move faster. Ground every decision in customer data and feedback from both audiences.
  • EMPOWER OTHERS: Recruit, develop, and retain a world-class engineering team. Build a culture of psychological safety, candid feedback, and career growth. Coach your engineers-from mid-level to staff-to reach their full potential and take on increasing ownership. Champion diversity, equity, and inclusion in every hiring and development decision.
  • RUTHLESSLY PRIORITIZE: Navigate competing priorities across external product features, internal platform needs, and Ops Tooling investments. Balance requests from multiple stakeholders-Product Management, internal engineering teams, and operations-with a clear framework for saying “no” to protect focus. Ensure resources are aligned to the highest-impact work across all three pillars.
  • WRITE IT DOWN: Communicate team strategy, progress, and risks clearly and consistently to engineering leadership and cross-functional partners. Author team plans, post-mortems, and decision documents that create transparency and alignment.
  • BUILD BRIDGES: Act as the primary point of contact between the Communication Identity Domain and its stakeholders. Manage relationships with Product Management, external-facing teams, and internal engineering teams that depend on your services and Ops Tooling. Proactively communicate roadmap plans, surface trade-offs, negotiate priorities, and ensure stakeholders have clear visibility into what your team is delivering and why.
  • NO SHENANIGANS: Model integrity in every interaction. Create an environment where engineers feel safe raising concerns, surfacing problems early, and challenging the status quo. Hold yourself and your team to the highest standards of ethical behavior.

Qualifications

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • 15+ years of software engineering experience with at least 5+ years in engineering management, leading a team of 10+ engineers and directly managing individual contributors.
  • Technical Depth: Strong hands-on background in designing and operating highly available, cloud-native distributed systems. You don’t need to write code daily, but you MUST be able to engage deeply in architectural reviews, evaluate technical proposals, and earn the trust of your senior engineers.
  • Cloud-Native Fluency: Deep familiarity with AWS ecosystems (Lambda, EKS, DynamoDB, Kafka), microservices patterns, and infrastructure-as-code practices (Kubernetes, Terraform).
  • AI-Forward Mindset: Demonstrated experience driving AI tool adoption within your engineering team. You should be able to articulate a clear vision for how AI accelerates your team’s delivery and quality.
  • Delivery Excellence: Proven track record of shipping complex software products on time and at high quality. Experience with agile methodologies and a data-driven approach to measuring team health and productivity.
  • People Leadership: A track record of building diverse, inclusive, high-performing engineering teams. Experience with career frameworks, performance management, and growing engineers from mid-level to staff-plus.
  • Clear Communication: Strong ability to communicate technical strategy, trade-offs, and team plans to engineering leadership, cross-functional partners, and your direct reports.
  • Stakeholder Management: Proven ability to manage relationships across multiple stakeholder groups with competing needs. Experience balancing external customer commitments with internal platform obligations and communicating trade-offs transparently.
  • Operational Rigor: Experience owning system reliability for mission-critical services, including incident management, on-call rotations, and SLO-driven operational improvements.

Desired:

  • Platform & Tooling Leadership: Experience leading a team that builds internal platforms or operational tooling serving other engineering teams, with a product mindset toward internal customers.
  • Team Scaling: Experience growing and evolving a team through periods of change, including onboarding new engineers, reshaping team processes, and managing through ambiguity.

Location

  1. This role will be remote, but is not eligible to be hired in San Francisco, CA, Oakland, CA, San Jose, CA, or the surrounding areas.

Travel

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

jobs.description:
Job Summary:
As the Head of Inventory Finance & Purchasing at Creative Chaos, you will oversee the financial planning and purchasing strategies that relate to inventory management. This includes ensuring the alignment of inventory levels with company objectives, optimizing procurement processes, and analyzing financial data related to inventory expenses to drive cost efficiencies. Your expertise in finance, combined with strong negotiation skills, will play a key role in maintaining an effective supply chain while maximizing profitability.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Core Responsibilities

End-to-End Purchasing Management

  • Own all purchasing activities across multiple product categories: nicotine products, non-nicotine products, accessories, apparel, POS materials, marketing collateral, and future product lines.
  • Source, evaluate, and manage multiple global vendors; negotiate pricing, terms, MOQs, and lead times.
  • Create and manage all POs, track confirmations, and follow up on delays, discrepancies, and quality issues

Vendor, Manufacturing & Logistics Coordination

    • Coordinate with international vendors, manufacturers, freight forwarders, and warehouse partners.
    • Track production timelines, shipping schedules, customs clearance, and delivery milestones.
    • Escalate any risks to supply continuity and propose mitigation plans proactively.

Inventory Planning & Forecast Alignment

    • Partner closely with FP&A to translate SKU-level revenue forecasts into purchase plans and replenishment schedules.
    • Build and maintain inventory models to prevent stockouts and avoid overstock
    • Monitor inbound inventory, open POs, transit times, and safety stock levels.

Inventory Monitoring, Controls & Reporting

    • Actively monitor inventory levels across all warehouses and 3PLs; identify hot spots, aging stock, and at-risk items.
    • Produce weekly and monthly inventory reports for management with actionable insights.
    • Flag and escalate issues involving shrinkage, discrepancies, expiry, or inaccurate receiving.

. Inventory Lifecycle & Accounting Ownership

    • Oversee the full lifecycle: receiving, costing, landed cost allocation, valuation, reconciliations, and adjustments.
    • Ensure accurate month-end close in QBO and all Shopify-integrated systems.
    • Maintain alignment between warehouse systems, ERP tools, Shopify, and finance.

Systems Implementation & Optimization

    • Lead the setup, configuration, and continuous improvement of inventory management platforms (ERP/WMS).
    • Ensure proper workflows, controls, item master data standards, and clean data migration.
    • Develop SOPs for purchasing, receiving, cycle counting, and inventory adjustments.

Cycle Counts, Physical Counts & Variance Resolution

    • Own cycle count schedules with warehouse partners and lead full physical counts.
    • Investigate and resolve discrepancies, working hands-on to identify root causes (system, vendor, warehouse, or process).
    • Implement stronger internal controls to reduce shrinkage, errors, and operational waste.

Financial Reporting, Analysis & Compliance

    • Prepare and analyze all inventory-related financial reports including:
    • Aging
    • Write-offs / obsolescence
    • Margin analysis
    • Landed cost reports
    • Audit schedules
    • Ensure clean, accurate, and reconcilable data flow between all systems (WMS, ERP, Shopify, QBO).
    • Support internal and external audits related to inventory and COGS.

Cross-Functional Leadership

    • Work closely with Sales, Marketing, FP&A, Product, Manufacturing, and Operations to stay ahead of demand trends and product launches.
    • Operate as the company’s subject-matter expert on inventory finance and purchasing strategy.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or a related field; a master's degree is preferred.
  • Minimum of 10 years of experience in finance or purchasing, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
  • Strong knowledge of inventory management principles and best practices.
  • Proven experience in financial analysis, budgeting, and forecasting.
  • Excellent negotiation and contract management skills.
  • Proficient in financial modeling and inventory management software.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience in a technology or creative industry is a plus.

Benefits

  • Paid Time Off
  • Health Insurance
  • OPD
  • Training and Development

jobs.excerpt: Position Summary – Accounting ManagerReports to: Director of Finance Department: Finance / AdministrationStatus: Full-time, ExemptLocation: Remote Position OverviewClean Energy Counsel, a mission-driven law firm dedicated to accelerating the world’s transition away from fossil fuels, seeks to hire a highly qualified accounting manager to join our firm.
jobs.description:
Position Summary – Accounting Manager

Reports to: Director of Finance

Department: Finance / Administration

Status: Full-time, Exempt

Location: Remote

Position Overview

Clean Energy Counsel, a mission-driven law firm dedicated to accelerating the world’s transition away from fossil fuels, seeks to hire a highly qualified accounting manager to join our firm. The Accounting Manager is responsible for the day-to-day management and execution of the Firm’s accounting operations under the direction of the Director of Finance. This position is responsible for maintaining the accuracy and integrity of the Firm’s financial records and ensuring that general ledger activity, account reconciliations, accounts payable, cash receipts and accounts receivable accounting, trust accounting, payroll-related accounting, month-end and year-end close activities, and financial schedules are completed accurately and timely.

The Accounting Manager serves as the operational leader for the accounting function, establishes and maintains consistent accounting workflows, supervises designated accounting staff, maintains appropriate supporting documentation and internal controls, and prepares financial statements and supporting information for review and analysis by the Director of Finance.

The position requires a hands-on accounting professional who can independently manage recurring accounting processes and deadlines, identify and resolve accounting issues, develop staff, and identify opportunities to improve accounting processes and controls.

Key Responsibilities

Accounting Operations & General Ledger

  • Own and manage the day-to-day execution of the Firm’s accounting operations.
  • Maintain the general ledger and ensure transactions are accurately, consistently, and timely recorded.
  • Prepare and post routine and approved adjusting journal entries.
  • Manage the monthly accounting close process and ensure required activities are completed according to established deadlines.
  • Prepare and/or review balance sheet reconciliations and supporting schedules.
  • Review general ledger activity and account balances for accuracy, completeness, and unusual or inconsistent activity.
  • Research and resolve accounting discrepancies and reconciling items.
  • Maintain appropriate documentation supporting accounting transactions, account balances, and reconciliations.
  • Escalate significant or unusual accounting matters requiring additional judgment to the Director of Finance.

Accounts Receivable Accounting & Cash Receipts

  • Maintain accurate accounts receivable accounting records following the posting of client invoices.
  • Manage the accounting and application of client payments, credits, write-offs, adjustments, and other accounts receivable activity.
  • Research and resolve unapplied cash and accounting discrepancies in coordination with Billing personnel.
  • Maintain appropriate accounting documentation supporting accounts receivable activity.
  • Provide accurate accounts receivable balances and supporting financial information to the Director of Finance and Billing function as needed.

Accounts Payable & Expense Administration

  • Manage day-to-day accounts payable operations and established payment processes.
  • Ensure invoices and employee reimbursements are properly documented, approved, coded, and processed.
  • Review vendor account activity and resolve discrepancies.
  • Maintain appropriate vendor records and supporting documentation.
  • Monitor payment deadlines and established cash-disbursement controls.
  • Review accounts payable work performed by accounting staff for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established procedures.
  • Maintain appropriate segregation of duties and controls over cash disbursements.

Cash & Bank Accounting

  • Maintain accurate accounting records for the Firm’s operating cash accounts.
  • Prepare or review bank and credit card reconciliations.
  • Research and resolve outstanding or unidentified transactions.
  • Maintain accurate records of cash receipts, deposits, transfers, and other banking activity.
  • Monitor outstanding checks and other reconciling items and ensure timely resolution.
  • Prepare cash balance and activity information for review and cash-flow analysis by the Director of Finance.
  • Assist with operational banking administration as assigned.

Trust Accounting

  • Manage or oversee recurring trust/IOLTA account reconciliations.
  • Maintain complete and accurate trust accounting records and supporting documentation.
  • Ensure trust transactions are properly recorded and processed in accordance with established Firm procedures.
  • Monitor trust balances and identify unusual, aged, or unreconciled items for review.
  • Maintain appropriate accounting controls over client and third-party funds.
  • Support compliance with applicable trust accounting requirements.
  • Promptly escalate trust accounting discrepancies or potential compliance concerns to the Director of Finance.

Payroll Accounting

  • Manage accounting activities associated with payroll processing.
  • Review and reconcile payroll-related general ledger accounts.
  • Ensure payroll activity is accurately recorded in the Firm’s accounting system.
  • Research payroll accounting discrepancies and coordinate corrections as necessary.
  • Maintain payroll-related accounting schedules and supporting documentation.
  • Provide payroll expense information and supporting data to the Director of Finance for financial reporting, budgeting, and analysis.

Month-End & Year-End Close Management

  • Own and coordinate the monthly accounting close process and close calendar.
  • Establish close deadlines and ensure required accounting activities are completed timely.
  • Prepare and review account reconciliations, accruals, journal entries, and supporting schedules required for close.
  • Review account balances and financial activity for accuracy, completeness, and unusual trends.
  • Resolve accounting discrepancies before completion of the close.
  • Prepare preliminary monthly financial statements and supporting schedules for review by the Director of Finance.
  • Coordinate accounting activities associated with the year-end close.
  • Prepare year-end reconciliations and supporting schedules.
  • Record approved year-end and tax adjustments and maintain appropriate supporting documentation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve the timeliness, accuracy, and efficiency of the close process.

Financial Reporting Preparation

  • Prepare recurring financial statements, management reports, schedules, and supporting financial information for review by the Director of Finance.
  • Ensure financial reports reconcile to the general ledger and underlying accounting records.
  • Maintain recurring reporting schedules and supporting documentation.
  • Prepare budget-to-actual reports and supporting account-level detail.
  • Provide historical financial information and accounting data used by the Director of Finance in budgeting and forecasting.
  • Research financial reporting discrepancies and ensure source data is complete and accurate.

Tax & Audit Support

  • Prepare accounting schedules, reconciliations, and supporting workpapers required for tax preparation and external audits.
  • Compile financial information requested by the Director of Finance, CPA, tax advisors, or auditors.
  • Prepare year-end tax workpapers and supporting accounting schedules.
  • Maintain documentation supporting tax payments and filings as directed.
  • Research accounting questions or discrepancies identified during tax preparation or audit activities.
  • Record approved audit and tax adjustments.

Internal Controls & Accounting Procedures

  • Execute and monitor accounting controls, policies, and procedures established in coordination with the Director of Finance.
  • Ensure accounting staff consistently follow established processes, approval requirements, and segregation-of-duties controls.
  • Document recurring accounting procedures and maintain current process documentation.
  • Identify control weaknesses, accounting risks, inefficiencies, or process gaps and recommend improvements to the Director of Finance.
  • Implement approved accounting process and control improvements.
  • Periodically review accounting workflows to ensure controls remain appropriate as the Firm grows.

Accounting Systems & Process Improvement

  • Serve as the operational lead for the Firm’s accounting systems.
  • Maintain accounting system data and oversee routine accounting-system administration.
  • Identify opportunities to improve accounting workflows, accuracy, efficiency, automation, and documentation.
  • Participate in implementation, testing, and training associated with new or modified financial systems.
  • Coordinate with the Billing function where billing-system activity interfaces with accounting records.
  • Assist the Director of Finance with finance-related technology and process improvement initiatives.

Staff Supervision & Development

  • Provide day-to-day supervision and direction to designated accounting personnel, including accounts payable, accounts receivable/cash receipts, payroll accounting, and other accounting staff as assigned.
  • Establish work priorities, responsibilities, and recurring accounting deadlines.
  • Review staff work for accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and compliance with established procedures.
  • Train, mentor, and develop accounting staff.
  • Establish and maintain appropriate cross-training and backup coverage for critical accounting functions.
  • Maintain clear documentation of departmental processes and responsibilities.
  • Identify staffing, training, workflow, and resource needs and communicate recommendations to the Director of Finance.
  • Foster accountability, collaboration, responsiveness, continuous improvement, and professional development within the accounting team.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive accounting experience, preferably including supervisory or team-lead responsibilities.
  • Law firm or professional services accounting experience strongly preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of general ledger accounting, account reconciliations, month-end and year-end close, accounts payable, accounts receivable accounting, cash management, and financial statement preparation.
  • Experience with law firm billing and trust accounting strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of GAAP and internal accounting controls.
  • Experience with trust/IOLTA accounting strongly preferred.
  • Experience with accounting and legal billing software such as QuickBooks, Clio, Elite, Aderant, or similar systems.
  • Strong Excel skills and ability to work effectively with complex financial data.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage recurring deadlines and multiple priorities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to effectively supervise, train, and develop accounting staff.

Core Competencies

  • Strong operational and technical accounting knowledge
  • Financial accuracy and attention to detail
  • Accountability and ownership
  • Organization and deadline management
  • Analytical and problem-solving ability
  • Effective staff supervision and development
  • Process improvement mindset
  • Sound judgment and appropriate escalation
  • Strong communication and collaboration
  • High integrity and commitment to confidentiality and ethical standards

Benefits

Benefits for this role include the following:

  • Base salary of $120,000-$150,000. The base salary for this position will be determined during the interview process and will vary based on multiple factors, including but not limited to geographical location, prior experience, relevant expertise, current business needs, and market factors.
  • Annual merit bonuses
  • Fully remote work environment with annual in-person retreat
  • 401(k), including firm profit-sharing matching
  • Dental/Health/Vision/Rx insurance
  • Paid time off and paid holidays

Who We Are

At Clean Energy Counsel, we provide the legal power to get sustainable projects developed, financed, and built – because speeding our transition away from fossil fuels is how we change the world’s trajectory for the better. Our team of attorneys gets deals closed and projects built because we care. Advancing clean energy isn’t just our job—it’s our hope for the future. Clean Energy Counsel gives attorneys the opportunity to do sophisticated, meaningful, industry-advancing work, all while leading a more balanced life in a work culture that values collaboration and respect. For clients, this translates to an extraordinary level of care, brought to bear for common cause. As the only mission-driven law firm solely focused on renewable energy, Clean Energy Counsel carries forward its unique model of advancing a sustainable future with sustainable law.

Our singular focus attracts the best talent in the industry, and we’ve built a deep and diverse bench of industry veterans who are passionate about their work and value our culture of respect and support.

We represent a diverse range of renewable energy project developers, investors, suppliers, and service providers across a full spectrum of technologies, including solar, energy storage, wind, energy efficiency, electric vehicles and charging infrastructure, waste to value, and sustainable infrastructure and materials - from Fortune 50 companies to start-ups.

Come As You Are

Our deep-rooted commitment to diversity and inclusion drives our ability to attract high-performing employees with diverse experience and perspectives who value a supportive work culture based on care and respect. That includes providing equal employment opportunities without consideration of race, color, religion, ethnicity, citizenship, political activity or affiliation, marital status, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, sex or gender, or any other basis protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.

Salary: $120k - $150k

Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that.

We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.

The Role

We're hiring Licensed Psychologists (Ph.D/Psy.D) to conduct autism assessments for adults via telehealth. You'll join a team dedicated to creating affordable, accessible diagnostic services while helping to shape best practices in adult autism assessment.

Our clinicians come from diverse backgrounds and career stages - whether you're building your career foundation, balancing work with other responsibilities, or expanding your clinical expertise, we offer flexibility to match your needs.

jobs.excerpt: About Us:Endpoint is an interactive response technology (IRT®) systems and solutions provider that supports the life sciences industry.
jobs.description:
About Us:

Endpoint is an interactive response technology (IRT®) systems and solutions provider that supports the life sciences industry. Since 2009, we have been working with a single vision in mind, to help sponsors and pharmaceutical companies achieve clinical trial success. Our solutions, realized through the proprietary PULSE® platform, have proven to maximize the supply chain, minimize operational costs, and ensure timely and accurate patient dosing. Endpoint is headquartered in Raleigh-Durham, North Carolina with offices across the United States, Europe, and Asia.

Position Overview:

The Project Manager is the primary client interface for client implementations, from initial engagement to study closedown. Project Managers are responsible for managing projects through the software development lifecycle and through study maintenance while working collaboratively with teammates and maintaining exceptional client satisfaction.

As a Project Manager, you are the primary point of contact for our clinical trial sponsor and CRO clients from the moment their Randomization and Trial Supply Management (RTSM) system goes live through the life of the study. You own the day-to-day client relationship, the project plan, and the coordination across internal teams needed to keep the trial's randomization and drug supply operations running smoothly.

This is a delivery and relationship-management role, not a system-build role: you inherit a validated, go-live-ready RTSM system from the BSA and study build team, and you are accountable for everything that happens with that system in production — change requests, user management, ongoing supply strategy conversations, issue triage, and study close-out.

*This position can be based remotely within UK*

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as the single point of contact for the client (sponsor/CRO) for all RTSM-related activities post go-live, building trusted, long-term relationships across the life of the study.

  • Lead recurring client status calls and steering committee meetings; own the agenda, minutes, and action item tracking.

  • Manage the end-to-end change control process for live systems: intake change requests, scope impact, coordinate with Design/Build, QA, and Biostatistics, and drive changes through validation and deployment.

  • Own the project plan, timeline, and RAID (risks, actions, issues, decisions) log for each assigned study post go-live.

  • Coordinate site and depot user provisioning, training refreshers, and access issues in partnership with the Help Desk and Training teams.

  • Monitor drug supply forecasting, inventory thresholds, and resupply strategy conversations with the client, escalating operational risk proactively.

  • Manage study amendments (protocol amendments, dosing changes, new sites/countries, IP updates) from client request through implementation.

  • Coordinate UAT (user acceptance testing) for any post-go-live system changes with the client and internal build teams.

  • Track and communicate study metrics (enrollment, randomization, supply status) to the client and internal leadership.

  • Own financial tracking for the account, including change order scoping, budget tracking, and invoicing coordination with the client and internal finance.

  • Lead study close-out activities: final reconciliation, system decommissioning, archival, and lessons-learned reviews.

  • Act as the internal advocate for the client, partnering with Sales, Design PM, Programming, QA, and Regulatory to resolve issues quickly.

  • Maintain audit-ready documentation in accordance with GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, and internal SOPs

Authority:

  • The Project Manager has the authority to assess and manage risks associated with assigned client IRT systems and change requests, and to make informed decisions and recommendations within defined project, client, and governance frameworks

Accountabilities:

  • Demonstrate consistent, accurate, and timely completion of all responsibilities.
  • Effectively utilise available resources to drive timely study delivery while maintaining clear oversight, accountability, and appropriate documentation.

Experience:

  • 2+ years of Project Management experience in clinical trials, RTSM/IRT, clinical supply chain, or a related life sciences/technology field

  • 2-4 years’ experience in the life science industry

  • Previous experience working in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment preferred.

  • Familiarity using SQL a plus

Skills:

  • Strong attention to detail and quality-focus

  • Strong customer service orientation

  • Excellent organizational and time management skills

  • Good communication skills

  • Excellent organizational skills

  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work effectively with a wide variety of professionals

  • Able to work on multiple assignments with moderate supervision

Endpoint Clinical does not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms or any other third parties. Any unsolicited resume sent to Endpoint Clinical will be considered Endpoint Clinical property, and Endpoint Clinical will not pay a fee should it hire the subject of any unsolicited resume.

jobs.description:
Processo de seleção desenvolvido pela matteria

Localização e modo de trabalho

Residência fixa em uma das capitais da Amazônia Legal brasileira - Remoto

Quem somos

A missão da The Nature Conservancy (TNC) é proteger as terras e as águas das quais toda a vida depende. Como uma organização baseada na ciência, criamos soluções inovadoras e práticas para os desafios mais difíceis do mundo, para que possamos criar um mundo no qual as pessoas e a natureza prosperem. Estamos enraizados em nossa Missão e guiados por nossos Valores, que incluem o Compromisso com a Diversidade e o Respeito às Pessoas, Comunidades e Culturas. Seja desenvolvimento de carreira, horários flexíveis ou uma missão gratificante, há muitas razões para amar a vida na TNC. Quer ter uma visão melhor da TNC? Confira nossa conta no instagram e o Relatório Anual 2024, além da #tncbrasil no LinkedIn.

Nosso objetivo é cultivar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo para que todos os nossos colegas em todo o mundo sintam um sentimento de pertencimento e que suas contribuições únicas para nossa missão sejam valorizadas. Sabemos que só alcançaremos nossa Missão contratando e engajando uma força de trabalho diversificada que reflita as comunidades em que trabalhamos. Além dos requisitos em nossas postagens, reconhecemos que as pessoas vêm com talento e experiências fora do trabalho. A diversidade de experiências e habilidades combinadas com paixão são a chave para a inovação e uma cultura de inclusão! Por favor, inscreva-se - adoraríamos ouvir de você. Para citar o que inúmeros membros da equipe da TNC dizem: “você se juntará por causa da nossa missão e ficará por nossas pessoas”.

Nosso impacto

  • 71 milhões de hectares: impacto positivo almejado até 2030, com foco em conservação e aprimoramento da gestão.

  • 187 mil km de rios: extensão para a qual a TNC Brasil busca promover soluções e políticas públicas de conservação até 2030.

  • 369 milhões de toneladas de CO₂: volume de emissões que a organização pretende capturar ou contribuir para reduzir até 2030.

  • 3,8 milhões de pessoas: público que a TNC Brasil pretende apoiar, com atenção especial a povos tradicionais e comunidades indígenas, ampliando sua participação em espaços decisórios e sua liderança na gestão dos territórios.

Na Amazônia, exemplos recentes ajudam a dimensionar essa atuação: um projeto de Pagamento por Serviços Ambientais na Terra do Meio envolve 14 territórios coletivos, 3 mil pessoas e 10 milhões de hectares sob proteção de uso sustentável.

Propósito do cargo

Liderar a estratégia da TNC na Amazônia Brasileira a partir de uma visão sistêmica do território, conciliando conservação e desenvolvimento socioeconômico. O desafio será conectar diferentes agendas, atores e investimentos para transformar estratégias em resultados concretos e escaláveis, capazes de manter a floresta em pé, promover uma produção responsável e gerar valor para as pessoas e comunidades da Amazônia.

Principais responsabilidades

  • Acompanhar e implementar a estratégia e a Teoria da Mudança da TNC para a Amazônia Brasileira, traduzindo a visão institucional em prioridades, iniciativas e resultados mensuráveis.

  • Liderar um portfólio amplo e diverso, conectando agendas de produção agropecuária sustentável, proteção e valorização da floresta em pé, povos indígenas e comunidades tradicionais, clima, mecanismos financeiros e políticas públicas.

  • Assegurar capacidade de implementação e entrega, transformando estratégias em resultados concretos, monitorando avanços e adaptando planos diante de mudanças de contexto.

  • Promover uma visão de desenvolvimento socioeconômico da Amazônia, articulando conservação e produção responsável e identificando alavancas econômicas capazes de valorizar a floresta em pé.

  • Identificar oportunidades para ampliar iniciativas bem-sucedidas, superando a lógica de projetos-piloto e promovendo soluções com potencial de transformação sistêmica e atuação em larga escala.

  • Construir e fortalecer relações estratégicas com governos estaduais e federal, setor privado, instituições financeiras, produtores, academia, organizações da sociedade civil, financiadores, povos indígenas, quilombolas, extrativistas e outras comunidades tradicionais.

  • Influenciar políticas públicas, estruturas de governança e processos de tomada de decisão relevantes para o desenvolvimento sustentável da Amazônia.

  • Liderar e apoiar a captação de recursos no Brasil e internacionalmente, mantendo um pipeline consistente de oportunidades e relacionamento estratégico com financiadores.

  • Supervisionar a gestão financeira e orçamentária de um portfólio de grande porte, assegurando uso eficiente dos recursos, sustentabilidade financeira e conformidade institucional.

  • Liderar gestores e equipes multidisciplinares, fortalecendo estruturas, responsabilidades, autonomia, accountability e capacidades técnicas e gerenciais.

  • Estimular integração e sinergia entre diferentes frentes de atuação, evitando silos e promovendo circulação de contexto e informação para qualificar a tomada de decisão.

  • Manter e fortalecer a agenda de diversidade, equidade e inclusão dentro da unidade, incorporando-a à liderança e à gestão da equipe.

  • Representar institucionalmente a TNC em fóruns, negociações e espaços estratégicos nacionais e internacionais.

Requisitos e competências para trabalhar conosco

Educação

  • Formação superior completa em áreas relacionadas à gestão de recursos naturais, políticas públicas, economia ou áreas afins. Pós-graduação em áreas correlatas será considerada desejável.

Experiência

  • Mínimo de 10 anos de experiência profissional em posições relacionadas a desenvolvimento socioeconômico, gestão de recursos naturais, políticas públicas, conservação ou áreas correlatas, com trajetória relevante em contextos complexos e de grande escala.

  • Experiência robusta na definição e implementação de estratégias, com responsabilidade por portfólios complexos, priorização de iniciativas, gestão de riscos e entrega de resultados mensuráveis.

  • Experiência comprovada na liderança de gestores e equipes multidisciplinares, incluindo desenvolvimento de talentos, estruturação de equipes e gestão de desempenho.

  • Trajetória de articulação multissetorial, estabelecendo relações e conduzindo negociações complexas com governos, setor privado, organizações da sociedade civil, comunidades, financiadores e outros atores estratégicos.

  • Experiência em relações governamentais e políticas públicas, incluindo capacidade de influenciar agendas, processos decisórios e condições institucionais necessárias para alcançar resultados em escala.

  • Experiência na gestão financeira e orçamentária de programas de grande porte, combinando visão estratégica com capacidade de acompanhamento da execução.

  • Experiência em captação de recursos e relacionamento com financiadores, contribuindo para a construção e manutenção de um pipeline de financiamento no Brasil e/ou internacionalmente.

  • Será especialmente valorizada uma trajetória que demonstre conhecimento e compreensão do contexto amazônico, incluindo suas dinâmicas socioeconômicas, produtivas, ambientais, políticas e territoriais.

  • Será um diferencial experiência com mecanismos financeiros, finanças estruturadas, setor privado ou desenvolvimento econômico, especialmente quando aplicada a desafios socioambientais e/ou territoriais.

    Conhecimento e habilidades

  • Visão sistêmica da Amazônia: capacidade de compreender o território para além de uma única agenda temática, conectando desenvolvimento socioeconômico, conservação, produção agropecuária, floresta, clima, povos e comunidades tradicionais, políticas públicas e investimentos.

  • Pensamento estratégico e de escala: capacidade de identificar as principais alavancas de transformação de um sistema e desenvolver soluções que possam avançar de iniciativas pontuais para resultados de maior escala.

  • Gestão e implementação: capacidade de transformar estratégia em execução, estabelecer prioridades, acompanhar resultados e replanejar recursos e ações diante de mudanças de contexto.

  • Articulação e negociação: habilidade para navegar entre interesses distintos, construir agendas comuns e mobilizar atores públicos, privados e sociais em torno de objetivos compartilhados.

  • Visão econômico-financeira: capacidade de compreender o papel de investimentos, mecanismos financeiros, setor privado e modelos econômicos na construção de soluções sustentáveis para a Amazônia.

  • Captação e mobilização de recursos: habilidade para desenvolver relações com financiadores, identificar oportunidades e contribuir estrategicamente para a sustentabilidade financeira do portfólio.

  • Inglês avançado, oral e escrito, considerando as interações, apresentações e eventos internacionais inerentes à posição. Inglês fluente é desejável e conhecimentos de espanhol serão considerados um diferencial.

Competências

  • Visão sistêmica e pensamento estratégico: conecta diferentes variáveis e agendas, compreende interdependências e mantém uma visão ampla do território sem perder a capacidade de priorização.

  • Orientação à implementação e resultados: transforma estratégia em ação, acompanha a execução e mantém foco consistente nas entregas e no impacto esperado.

  • Liderança adaptativa: lidera com segurança em contextos de incerteza e complexidade, sendo capaz de rever planos, redirecionar prioridades e mobilizar o time diante de mudanças.

  • Influência e construção de consensos: estabelece relações de confiança e consegue aproximar atores com interesses e perspectivas distintas.

  • Liderança de pessoas: desenvolve equipes fortes e tecnicamente qualificadas, compartilha contexto, promove autonomia e evita a formação de silos na tomada de decisão.

  • Colaboração e integração: consegue navegar por um portfólio diverso sem precisar ser especialista em todas as temáticas, conectando conhecimentos, pessoas e iniciativas para gerar sinergias.

  • Proatividade e senso de protagonismo: antecipa necessidades, identifica oportunidades e mobiliza recursos e pessoas para fazer a estratégia avançar.

  • Compromisso com diversidade, equidade e inclusão: incorpora essa agenda à forma de liderar, desenvolver equipes e construir uma cultura organizacional inclusiva.

Perfil de nossa equipe

A The Nature Conservancy é enraizada em nossa missão e guiada por nossos valores. Temos o compromisso de cultivar um ambiente de trabalho inclusivo, onde todos os colegas ao redor do mundo sintam um senso de pertencimento e tenham suas contribuições únicas valorizadas. Nosso objetivo é construir uma força de trabalho diversa que reflita as comunidades em que atuamos, reconhecendo que a diversidade de experiências e habilidades é fundamental para a inovação.

“Você vai se juntar a nós pela nossa missão — e vai ficar pelas nossas pessoas.”

Principais interesses para trabalhar conosco

O candidato ideal será motivado pela oportunidade de causar um impacto direto nos esforços globais de conservação.

Deve ter um forte interesse em sustentabilidade ambiental, proteção da biodiversidade e conservação de ecossistemas críticos no Brasil.

This role leads acquisition, disposition, leasing, portfolio planning, and acting as the primary liaison with landlords, tenants, brokers, and internal stakeholders.

The ideal candidate is a self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys building relationships with technical professionals, and can effectively partner with hiring managers to attract and hire top talent.   • 4-6 years of technical recruiting in the federal government contracting space.

The Executive Order on Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government, issued on January 20, 2021, aims to address systemic barriers and promote equal opportunity for underserved communities and individuals in the United States. The order emphasizes the importance of advancing equity, civil rights, racial justice, and equal opportunity across all federal agencies. It directs agencies to assess their programs and policies for perpetuating systemic barriers and develop strategies to deliver resources and benefits equitably to all. The order also establishes an interagency working group to gather and analyze data to inform efforts to measure and advance equity. Additionally, it revokes previous executive orders that were seen as hindering progress in this area.
